sections.heading: 4. Reconcile the evidence pipeline to Formula v2.0 and daily controls
paragraphs: Keep the scorecard bridge visible in every dashboard. Conservative gross billings of $150,000 less 35% upstream cost of $52,500 leave $97,500 retained contribution; subtract the $70,500 residual cost allowance to reach $27,000 owner profit. Base gross billings of $675,000 less $236,250 upstream cost leave $438,750 retained contribution; subtract $249,750 to reach $189,000. Scaled gross billings of $1,200,000 less $420,000 upstream cost leave $780,000; subtract $324,000 to reach $456,000. Those profits equal 18%, 28.0%, and 38% of gross billings, or 27.69%, 43.08%, and 58.46% of retained contribution after rounding. Use the supplied 65% retained-share convention consistently, while applying ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to actual contracts rather than treating a spreadsheet percentage as an accounting conclusion. Agent arrangements generally report the applicable net fee, while principal arrangements require their own gross presentation analysis. Customer application sales, merchant transaction volume, and unrelated underlying business activity never enter this desk's revenue. Neither does the face value of unused prepaid service credit automatically become earned revenue. The unit examples above explain selection mechanics; their individual spreads are not substitutes for the canonical annual scenario mix or retained-share assumption.

Do not force the stated $2,000–$14,000 monthly operating-expense range to equal every residual cost in the annual scenarios. The scorecard arithmetic implies monthly residual allowances of $5,875, $20,812.50, and $27,000 after upstream cost and before owner profit. Because the latter two exceed the stated operating range, obtain an explicit bridge for staffing, contractors, selling expense, payment costs, reserves, and other included buckets; do not invent allocations. Keep the team assumptions unchanged at one full-time operator plus two contractors for Conservative and Base, and two full-time operators plus three contractors for Scaled. Startup capital remains $10,000–$60,000 and time to first deal remains one to four months. Track cash exposure independently of reported margin: a prepaid customer wallet can reduce collection risk while a noncancelable bare-metal commitment still drains cash during idle weeks. Build a daily utilization forecast from purchased device-hours, qualified booked demand, and contract expiry dates. Stress GPU generation price compression and simultaneous customer departures before renewing capacity. For telecom, stress destination mix shifts and newly effective surcharges. When the resulting cash requirement exceeds the funded reserve, reduce new commitments rather than disguising idle capacity as an enrichment or marketing expense.

Run the production pipeline as a small set of accountable services: registry collector, evidence store, pricing engine, prepaid ledger, dispatch controller, metering reconciler, and exception queue. Python's sqlite3 supports an initial single-writer evidence store, while hashlib, urllib.request, json, and scheduled jobs support straightforward collection without an oversized integration stack. Move operational concurrency to a suitable transactional database when needed; the chapter's module itself requires no external packages. Keep credentials outside exported evidence, scope each connector narrowly, and log identifiers rather than customer payloads. Test restored backups, replayed webhooks, stale rate decks, missing GPU counters, and duplicated call records before increasing volume. Screen prohibited mining, abusive calling, and unsupported messaging patterns against documented acceptable-use rules, with bounded review and a working suspension path. Apply 47 U.S.C. 227 and implementing calling rules to the actual traffic, not merely to the customer's campaign registration. Track false-positive suspensions alongside confirmed abuse so controls remain measurable. Finish each day with three reconciliations: customer usage to customer charges, upstream usage to supplier charges, and processor movements to wallet liabilities. Any unexplained difference receives an owner, amount, age, and next action. Information becomes an edge only when it changes a reproducible purchase, price, or stop decision.

sections.heading: 1. Classify each service before accepting a customer order
paragraphs: Start with a service inventory, not a single label such as technology reseller. A dedicated H100 lease, a metered inference endpoint, outbound SIP termination, application-to-person messaging, and an IPv4 sublease create different obligations even when one Stripe invoice collects payment. Identify the contracting seller, upstream supplier, customer location, traffic destination, numbering responsibility, and party controlling service delivery. Pure compute hosting does not become telecommunications merely because packets traverse a network. Conversely, buying carrier termination wholesale does not remove provider duties when the operator sells covered voice services under their own name. For voice, map the offering against 47 U.S.C. 153 and the applicable FCC service definitions; evaluate Section 214 authority under 47 U.S.C. 214 and 47 CFR Part 63, including whether international service requires separate authority. Determine FCC Form 499-A registration and reporting duties from actual activities and current filing instructions. A contribution exemption does not automatically eliminate filing duties. Record who owns each filing, its supporting revenue classification, and the next review date. Keep compute and telecom order forms separable so that adding messaging does not silently expand a GPU customer's service scope or cause unrelated usage to inherit unsuitable suspension and billing terms.

Treat STIR/SHAKEN, the Robocall Mitigation Database, and messaging registration as separate systems with separate evidence. Under 47 CFR 64.6301 and 64.6305, determine the obligations attached to the operator's actual voice-provider or intermediate-provider role, including authentication, mitigation, filing, and traffic acceptance requirements where applicable. Do not describe a supplier's database entry as the reseller's filing. Verify upstream status and require timely traceback cooperation, customer investigation, and route suspension rights. A signed call is not proof that its recipient authorized it; attestation and consumer permission answer different questions. For 10DLC, The Campaign Registry and carrier campaign vetting are industry onboarding mechanisms, not federal licenses and not substitutes for TCPA analysis. Capture the actual brand, use case, opt-in language, sample messages, help response, and opt-out behavior before submitting a campaign. Prohibit moving rejected traffic to another aggregator to bypass restrictions. Configure least-cost routing to consider destination, quality, permitted traffic, and supplier eligibility before price. If an eligible route costs more than the customer's ceiling, pause delivery or obtain a revised order rather than silently routing through an unsuitable carrier. Preserve traceability without retaining message content longer than the documented purpose requires.

Build a jurisdiction worksheet around where customers and end users receive service, not merely the operator's incorporation state. California Public Utilities Code 1001 illustrates why facilities, service classification, and state commission authority require a separate analysis; it does not establish that every cloud application needs a telephone certificate. Check state registration, numbering, emergency-calling, accessibility, tax, and surcharge requirements against the specific product. Interconnected VoIP can trigger duties that a non-interconnected software feature does not. Florida Statutes 501.059 adds state telephone-solicitation constraints that cannot be replaced by a national campaign template. California consumer-data processing can require service-provider or contractor terms under Civil Code 1798.100 and related provisions, depending on the parties and thresholds. Maintain separate tax mappings for compute, telecommunications, and messaging rather than assuming a software tax code fits everything. Screen customer identity, beneficial ownership where warranted, destination, and intended use against applicable sanctions restrictions; GPU hardware, software, technical transfers, and restricted end uses may also require export-control analysis. Do not represent every cloud GPU session as a hardware export. Escalate facts that change the classification, and keep the affected destination or service disabled until the required permissions and operating responsibilities are established.

sections.heading: 2. Make data, acceptable use, and supplier promises enforceable
paragraphs: A compute order should identify GPU model, physical or virtual allocation, memory entitlement, scheduling policy, region, maintenance windows, and permitted substitution. H100, H200, and B200 capacity are not interchangeable simply because a dashboard displays GPU hours. Specify whether a slice provides hardware partitioning, time sharing, or exclusive access, and describe the isolation actually implemented. Run vLLM behind tenant-scoped credentials and apply authorization before LiteLLM chooses a provider. Avoid shared caches that expose another customer's prompts, embeddings, adapters, or generated output. Use DCGM for device health and utilization evidence, but define a separate customer billing meter; device utilization alone does not establish billable reserved time or accepted tokens. The acceptable-use schedule should prohibit unauthorized access, malware deployment, abusive mining where supplier terms prohibit it, unlawful content processing, and abusive calling or messaging. Specify investigative access, evidence preservation, immediate isolation for active harm, notice when appropriate, and restoration conditions. Customer screening is a risk-control process, not a claim that every compute reseller is subject to bank-style identification duties. Request identity and business purpose proportionate to service risk, and avoid accumulating sensitive identity documents without a defined need, restricted access, and deletion schedule.

Translate zero-data-retention promises into a data-flow schedule covering request bodies, responses, cache entries, tracing, crash dumps, abuse systems, support tickets, and backups. An operator cannot promise enterprise payload deletion while a fallback inference provider retains prompts for product improvement. Require explicit upstream settings or written terms supporting the promise, and remove ineligible endpoints from the routing pool rather than hoping a preferred route always succeeds. Distinguish payload retention from minimal billing and security metadata; disclose their fields, purpose, retention period, and access controls. Document any mandatory preservation exception narrowly instead of marketing absolute deletion that the contract contradicts. For health-sector customers, evaluate whether the service creates a business associate relationship under 45 CFR 160.103 and whether agreements under 45 CFR 164.504(e) are required. A business associate agreement is useful only when the selected infrastructure can perform its obligations. For covered telecommunications customer information, evaluate 47 U.S.C. 222 and the implementing FCC requirements separately from a general privacy policy. Test log suppression using synthetic sensitive markers, verify backups and support exports, and retain the test result. Failed deletion or accidental payload capture should trigger the incident procedure and customer notice assessment specified in the data-processing schedule.

Allocate intellectual-property rights by asset rather than saying that everything belongs to the customer. The customer retains rights in supplied data, weights, adapters, and prompts to the extent they possess those rights; the operator receives only the permissions needed to provide the service. Generated-output rights remain subject to applicable law and upstream model terms, so do not promise exclusive ownership merely because inference was paid. Identify the operator's pre-existing orchestration code, templates, and metering logic, and prohibit training on customer content unless a separate affirmative agreement permits it. Require customers to hold necessary model and dataset licenses without claiming this transfers the operator's own responsibilities. For IPv4 capacity, identify address blocks, permitted announcements, relevant registry policies, routing authorization, abuse contacts, and return procedures; possession of an invoice does not establish routing authority. Set a remediation period for reputation damage where safe, and reserve prompt isolation for active abuse. When a supplier terminates capacity, provide an orderly export or migration path for customer-controlled artifacts without exposing another tenant's information. The practical fallback is fewer eligible services with enforceable promises, not a broader catalog whose data, licensing, and routing obligations cannot be satisfied by the actual delivery chain.

callout.title: Protect the spread at the supplier boundary
callout.body: Experienced operators purchase enforceable rights and observable service behavior, not merely an attractive capacity quote.
items: Attach the supplier's precise retention configuration to each enterprise order; exclude unsupported LiteLLM fallbacks automatically.
Separate DCGM health telemetry from invoice evidence so a busy device does not become an invented customer charge.
Negotiate GPU substitution and maintenance credits before accepting long commitments; require customer permission for materially different hardware.
Keep a prequalified voice route with verified provider status and agreed traffic rules; price resilience before a carrier suspension occurs.

sections.heading: 3. Tie fees, liability, and exit rights to the canonical economics
paragraphs: Use the Formula v2.0 scorecard as a reconciliation framework, not a license to classify accounting revenue by preference. Conservative gross billings of $150,000 leave $97,500 at the stipulated 65% retained share; subtracting $70,500 of remaining modeled costs produces $27,000 owner profit. Base gross billings of $675,000 leave $438,750; subtracting $249,750 produces $189,000. Scaled gross billings of $1,200,000 leave $780,000; subtracting $324,000 produces $456,000. The corresponding upstream allocations are $52,500, $236,250, and $420,000. Owner-profit margins on gross billings are 18%, 28.0%, and 38%; margins on retained contribution are 27.69%, 43.08%, and 58.46%. These are different denominators, not competing versions of the same percentage. ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis depends on control and the actual arrangement; a 65% modeling factor does not independently establish net presentation. Maintain gross customer collections, supplier pass-throughs, retained contribution, and recognized revenue in separate ledger views. The advertised monthly operating-expense range is not an exhaustive reconciliation of every annual modeled cost. Keep workload examples below separate from these canonical scenarios, and never count customer application sales, token-user commerce, or downstream merchant volume as the operator's own billings.

Define the fee trigger before configuring the wallet. For reserved GPU capacity, billing can attach to the contracted reservation interval even when utilization is low; for token services, define accepted input and output units, tokenizer version, retries, and treatment of failed requests. For SIP, state destination rate decks, connection charges, minimum duration, rounding increments, and rate-change notice. For messaging, distinguish segments, carrier surcharges, registration charges, and delivery status. Illustratively, 1,000 accepted GPU-hours billed at $3.00 produce $3,000 gross; a $1.05 supplier cost per hour produces $1,050 upstream cost and $1,950 retained contribution, before remaining expenses. Those assumed rates illustrate the 65% factor and are not market quotes. Require a prepaid balance, authorize expected consumption atomically, settle measured usage, and release unused authorization. Stripe payment success does not eliminate chargebacks or make funds irrevocable. Prevent concurrent requests from overspending the same balance, and specify service suspension, residual-balance refunds, disputed usage, and abandoned-property treatment where applicable. Keep credits nontransferable and limited to the operator's own services unless a separate stored-value analysis supports broader functionality. A wallet protects collections; it cannot repair an uneconomic bare-metal commitment or replace an enforceable customer reservation.

Make the commercial allocation readable enough that sales, support, and engineering implement the same agreement. Scope belongs in the order form; usage definitions and fee triggers belong in the pricing schedule; availability calculations, exclusions, and credits belong in the service schedule. Limit anti-circumvention to identified introductions, a defined service opportunity, a reasonable period, and documented damages or an enforceable fee mechanism. Do not use it to block independent customer relationships or conceal supplier identity needed for security review. Negotiate a stated liability cap with explicit treatment of confidentiality, data incidents, intellectual-property claims, unpaid fees, and conduct that applicable law prevents parties from limiting. Avoid assuming supplier caps automatically cover the operator's broader promises. Specify notice addresses, escalation deadlines, governing law, forum or arbitration mechanics, and a practical method for disputing meter records. Evaluate UCC Article 2 only where the transaction and jurisdiction support its application; cloud services are not automatically sales of goods. Renewal should require clear notice and a defined cancellation path. Provide export timing, artifact format, deletion confirmation, number portability where applicable, and treatment of unused prepaid funds. Price these duties into the spread before signing, especially when upstream capacity renews earlier than the customer's reservation.

sections.heading: 4. Use evidence-backed comparisons and permission-aware outreach scripts
paragraphs: The mapped play competitor_intent_comparison_hijacking targets high-intent comparison, pricing, and cancellation searches through genuinely useful decision pages. Build text-only nominative comparisons using dated public pricing citations, matched units, region, commitment duration, hardware generation, and workload constraints. Nominative fair use is fact-dependent and varies by jurisdiction; using a competitor's name does not authorize confusion about source, sponsorship, or affiliation. Evaluate false-association and advertising risk under 15 U.S.C. 1125(a), and substantiate objective claims under the FTC Act. Do not copy logos, imitate account portals, suggest endorsement, or publish cancellation instructions that require a customer's credentials. A migration guide should explain how the customer exports their own artifacts through official interfaces. Illustratively, 200 qualified monthly visits at the play's 10–18% conversion assumption produce 20–36 conversions. If each conversion is an activated customer buying $200 of service, gross billings are $4,000–$7,200 and retained contribution at 65% is $2,600–$4,680 before acquisition and operating expenses. If conversion means a form submission instead, these billings cannot be claimed without a separate activation rate. The fallback is narrower text-only comparison coverage, timestamped public sources, and suspended claims when equivalent current pricing cannot be verified.

Separate commercial email from calling and messaging workflows because their permission rules differ. CAN-SPAM, 15 U.S.C. 7704, governs commercial email requirements including accurate headers, nondeceptive subjects, required advertising identification, a valid postal address, and a working opt-out honored within the statutory period. It does not create blanket permission to send automated sales texts. Under 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200, analyze the actual calling technology, message content, destination, consent, and applicable do-not-call requirements; business recipients and manually initiated calls do not erase every federal or state restriction. Check state rules before selecting calling hours or recording discovery sessions. Store the recipient's relevant consent evidence, source, timestamp, permitted sender, and requested channel rather than treating a purchased lead list as authorization. The scripts below are exact spoken or written bodies, not a substitute for production sender identification, postal-address fields, unsubscribe controls, or jurisdiction-specific disclosures. Deploy scripts only after the relevant contact eligibility check. Honor a stop request across connected systems promptly, and prevent a CRM resynchronization from reactivating suppression records. When permission cannot be established, use search content or a requested reply instead of switching channels to continue unwanted outreach.

Discovery should expose contractual mismatches before anyone quotes a cheaper unit rate. Ask whether GPU spend purchases exclusive reservations or interruptible consumption, whether prompts may leave a named region, whether outputs include protected health information, and whether the customer needs payload retention disabled across every fallback. For voice, ask who supplies numbers, originates traffic, obtains permission, answers traceback requests, and bears emergency-service duties where applicable. For messaging, inspect the opt-in journey and campaign use case rather than accepting a screenshot of a registration status alone. Quote a pilot with a wallet ceiling, named units, a stop condition, and a documented migration path. An illustrative $300 prepaid GPU pilot at $3.00 per accepted hour funds 100 hours; at the assumed $1.05 upstream rate, its $195 retained contribution is not owner profit. If the customer needs a $4.00 eligible route under a $3.00 price ceiling, pause or revise the order rather than quietly accepting a negative spread. Record objections as concrete constraints, not permission to exaggerate availability or savings. Send a written recap identifying assumptions, evidence still required, and excluded services. The strongest close is a bounded test whose bill, retention behavior, and exit procedure match the signed schedules.

sections.heading: 1. Turn Fifteen Plays into a Bounded Event System
paragraphs: Build one event spine rather than a collection of autonomous agents. A Python HTTPS handler receives supplier updates, buyer forms, payment notifications, and provisioning callbacks; durable storage records each event before acknowledging acceptance. Use an envelope containing event_id, tenant_id, event_type, occurred_at, schema_version, source_reference, and payload_digest. A uniqueness constraint on source plus event_id prevents duplicate work, while an outbox publishes tasks only after the corresponding transaction commits. Workers claim tasks with leases and bounded retries; expired leases return work to the queue without repeating an external purchase. Keep credentials in a managed secret store, separate tenant authorization from event routing, and reject unrecognized event versions. The full-time operator owns commercial exceptions and weekly economics. One contractor owns infrastructure reliability; the other owns carrier operations and evidence review. The fifteen-play mapping here comprises seven intake plays in the first matrix, seven fulfillment plays in the second, and the supplied citation-distribution play in section three. The descriptive local labels organize implementation; they do not assert additional canonical catalog identifiers. Every play produces an evidence record, a bounded proposed action, and an explicit recovery state. A stalled worker must never silently become a successful customer order.

Automate research through permitted APIs, supplier exports, and monitored rate sheets, not unrestricted browser agents with purchasing authority. Normalize H100, H200, and B200 offers by memory capacity, interconnect, region, tenancy, minimum term, cancellation rights, and actual available inventory. Store quoted timestamps because an attractive hourly price without a valid delivery window is not executable capacity. For SIP, retain destination prefixes, billing increments, setup charges, route restrictions, and effective dates; for IPv4, verify delegated control, permitted subleasing, routing support, and reputation history. An LLM may extract candidate fields into a fixed JSON schema, but deterministic validators enforce currencies, units, and required evidence links. Treat supplier documents as untrusted data: embedded instructions cannot modify system rules or invoke tools. An illustrative quote-analysis run costs $0.006 for extraction, $0.002 for validation infrastructure, and $0.002 for storage and delivery, totaling $0.010 before human review. At 3,000 runs monthly, direct automation costs $30. Compare that with the measured exception burden rather than calling the entire research function free. If a supplier changes its format, quarantine the affected feed and preserve the last verified offer with its original expiry. Never extend that expiry merely to keep a comparison page populated.

Define the automation denominator before celebrating productivity. In an illustrative weekly cohort of 1,000 eligible repetitive tasks, 740 finish without human execution and 260 require review, producing a 74% straight-through rate. Tasks count only after their output passes validation and reaches its intended system; failed retries, empty summaries, and duplicate callbacks do not count again. At six manual minutes per task, the counterfactual workload is 100 hours. If the 260 exceptions consume four minutes each and a 5% sample of the 740 automated completions consumes two minutes each, human handling takes 18.57 hours before maintenance and incident work. This is an illustrative capacity calculation, not a measured staffing result. Track exception rates separately for research, qualification, fulfillment, and acquisition so easy enrichment cannot conceal broken provisioning. Qualification rules should reject absent prepaid funding, prohibited resale terms, incompatible retention requirements, and unsupported calling uses before producing a quote. Human review remains mandatory for new minimum commitments, unusual identity evidence, privileged access, and consequential public claims. Suspend the affected automation when sampled errors exceed its agreed tolerance, even if overall throughput looks healthy. The purpose is fewer repeated decisions, not fewer people noticing expensive mistakes.

callout.body: Small teams win when each exception arrives with enough context to resolve it once.

sections.heading: 2. Connect Prepaid Money, Metered Service, and Safe Fulfillment
paragraphs: Treat Stripe as the payment processor, not as the authoritative usage ledger. Verify webhook signatures against the raw request body, apply replay protections, and record each processor event once. Payment states differ by payment method, so credit service balances only under a documented funding policy that accounts for delayed settlement and disputes. Maintain an append-only ledger separating funded credits, reserved credits, consumed credits, reversals, and adjustments. Before dispatching a request, atomically reserve its maximum permitted charge using the pricing version attached to the quote. Finalization replaces the reservation with measured consumption and releases the unused remainder; duplicate completion events must have no additional effect. For an illustrative $100 funded account, a $3 reservation leaves $97 available. If the completed job costs $2.40, consumption becomes $2.40 and available funds become $97.60. A worker timeout does not prove that upstream execution stopped, so do not release its hold until cancellation or usage reconciliation establishes the outcome. Place unresolved reservations in an age-based exception queue. Humans authorize refunds and disputed balance adjustments, while automated service suspension follows the agreed account policy. Keep all prices in integer minor currency units or explicit fixed-point decimal arithmetic.

Place LiteLLM behind authenticated tenant endpoints and route only among providers permitted by the customer's region, model, retention, and quality requirements. vLLM serves self-hosted inference pools; NVIDIA DCGM supplies hardware telemetry, including utilization and device health, rather than a complete customer billing system. Attribute usage through scheduler allocation records and request identifiers, then reconcile those records with inference token counts and infrastructure invoices. Hardware partitioning is generation- and configuration-dependent: validate supported isolation rather than treating every GPU slice as an equivalent security boundary. An illustrative million-token bundle sells for $10 and consumes $3.50 in upstream service, leaving $6.50 before other costs, consistent with the scorecard's aggregate 65% retained share. This example is a normalized bundle, not a vendor price quotation. A $0.70 fallback retry reduces that bundle's retention to $5.80; aggregate economics therefore need measured retry budgets. Use circuit breakers for timeouts, token inflation, and provider errors. Never fail over to a provider that violates a zero-data-retention commitment merely because it is available. When no eligible route remains, return an explicit capacity failure and reconcile the reservation against actual billable work. Separate control-plane metadata from customer prompts throughout recovery.

Automated least-cost routing must optimize acceptable completion cost, not the cheapest advertised SIP minute. A route selling 1,000 minutes for $20 with $7 upstream termination leaves $13 before other costs; setup fees, duration rounding, and failed-call charges can erase that illustrative spread. Use destination-specific cost ceilings alongside answer-seizure ratio, average call duration, post-dial delay, and fraud signals. These metrics are diagnostic, not proof that traffic is legitimate. Authenticate customers, restrict destinations, apply account velocity limits, and suspend suspected abuse for review. STIR/SHAKEN attestation reflects provider knowledge and authorization; it is not a legitimacy certificate. Determine actual provider roles under 47 CFR 64.6301 and 64.6305 before assigning authentication and Robocall Mitigation Database duties. For 10DLC, submit accurate brand and campaign evidence through supported provider interfaces; The Campaign Registry registration does not replace recipient permission or TCPA requirements. Poll asynchronous provisioning states and expose rejection reasons to a reviewer instead of repeatedly resubmitting altered identities. Review FCC Form 499-A obligations against the actual telecommunications offering and applicable exemptions. A failed messaging registration should leave the account inactive for that use case, not divert its traffic onto unrelated numbers.

sections.heading: 3. Compound Distribution with Verifiable Comparisons and Referrals
paragraphs: Implement llm_citation_geo_poisoning, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) & AI-Overview Citation Seeding, TRACK_2, as evidence-led publication, not corrupted retrieval or fabricated authority. Observe the public citations returned by ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews for commercial buyer questions about GPU rental, inference costs, and telecom capacity. Results vary by geography, session, and time; record the prompt, observation date, cited URL, visible answer, and comparison claim. Inspect only accessible results through permitted interfaces. Identify trade publications and technical directories that repeatedly support relevant answers, then seek authorized editorial contributions or dataset placements on those domains. Never impersonate a publisher or insert instructions intended to override an AI system. Publish visible tables with entity names, test conditions, dated prices, and source links; matching schema.org JSON-LD describes the same public content. An illustrative monthly study covers 40 prompts across four surfaces and two observations, yielding 320 observations. At $0.05 permitted retrieval and extraction cost per observation, direct processing costs $16 before editorial labor or access subscriptions. The fallback is strictly factual structured tables, matching markup, and corroborated placements across independent trade publications. Citation inclusion remains an observed outcome, never a purchased certainty.

Make programmatic pages useful enough to survive without search traffic. Generate comparisons only for combinations with current evidence: accelerator generation, region, contract term, model family, and retention option. A page comparing H200 reserved capacity with on-demand H100 must disclose workload and interconnect differences instead of claiming direct equivalence. Publish benchmark scripts, input dimensions, concurrency, latency percentiles, and observation dates; remove customer prompts and identifying telemetry. A deterministic renderer should block stale prices and unsupported claims before a human approves a new template or material revision. For an illustrative cohort, 2,000 qualified visits produce 100 calculator starts at 5%, 20 funded trials at 20%, and five repeat accounts at 25%. At $300 monthly gross billings each, those accounts produce $1,500 gross and $975 retained contribution before other costs. A $600 content and distribution expense therefore has a 0.62-month contribution payback only if the cohort sustains that activity; it is not owner profit. Track refunds, churn, and support burden by acquisition source. If organic visibility disappears, the same calculators should support partner referrals and sales conversations, preserving utility without inventing pages for combinations the operation cannot deliver.

Build the viral loop around optional sharing of useful, sanitized artifacts. A customer can export a benchmark comparison or cost report with a referral link after reviewing the exact public content; keep publication off by default. The report must not expose prompts, phone numbers, address assignments, traffic patterns, or negotiated supplier terms. Issue referral rewards only under published terms after collected revenue clears the relevant review period, and distinguish account credit from cash compensation. For outbound, use permissioned partner lists or appropriately sourced business contacts, preserve provenance, and apply suppression before every send. CAN-SPAM requirements under 15 U.S.C. 7704 apply to covered commercial email, including accurate headers, required identification, and functioning opt-out handling; do not reuse email eligibility as permission for automated calls or texts. An illustrative 200-message batch at $0.02 processing and delivery per message costs $4 before data and labor. Ten replies, three qualified conversations, and one funded account are hypotheses to test, not expected outcomes. Human reviewers approve claims, new audience definitions, and first batches. If complaints increase or source rights become uncertain, stop the affected sequence and investigate rather than rotating domains or identities.

sections.heading: 4. Reconcile the Scorecard and Rehearse Expensive Failures
paragraphs: Anchor automation spending to the canonical Formula v2.0 scenarios, not a newly invented growth forecast. Conservative gross billings are $150,000, upstream commitments consume $52,500, and retained revenue is $97,500. Subtract $70,500 of remaining modeled costs to reach $27,000 owner profit: 18% of gross billings and 27.69% of retained revenue. Base gross billings of $675,000 less $236,250 upstream produce $438,750 retained revenue; remaining costs of $249,750 leave $189,000, or 28.0% gross-basis and 43.08% retained margin. Scaled gross billings of $1,200,000 less $420,000 upstream produce $780,000 retained revenue; $324,000 remaining costs leave $456,000, or 38% gross-basis and 58.46% retained margin. These remaining-cost amounts are reconciliation residuals, not invented expense-category budgets. Do not equate them with the separate $2,000–$14,000 monthly operating-expense range. Startup capital remains $10,000–$60,000, with first deal timing of one to four months. Conservative and Base use 1 FT + 2 C; Scaled uses 2 FT + 3 C. Use the supplied 65% retained presentation consistently, while documenting actual ASC 606 principal-versus-agent conclusions by contract rather than assuming one universal recognition treatment.

Instrument unit costs at the run level and reconcile them monthly to actual invoices. Record model charges, retrieval charges, workflow infrastructure, payment processing, verification fees, carrier provisioning fees, and retry spend separately. For an illustrative 10,000 monthly automation runs at $0.012 direct cost each, infrastructure and model spend is $120. If 15% require three minutes of review at an assigned $40 hourly labor value, reviewer effort costs $3,000; effective cost becomes $0.312 per run before other overhead. That 15% example describes a specific workflow, not the earlier all-task 26% exception cohort. Compare equal scopes and include maintenance before deciding that a cheaper model improves economics. A model saving $30 while adding two review hours destroys $50 of value at that labor rate. Monitor utilization against break-even committed capacity, not just GPU occupancy graphs. Reserved supply remains payable when demand falls, while accelerator-generation price compression can reduce the resale price before contracts expire. Require owner review for longer commitments and revise quote expiries when supplier spreads narrow. Keep acquisition contribution, service contribution, and owner profit as separate dashboard layers so growing traffic cannot conceal a deteriorating book.

Rehearse failures with synthetic tenants and controlled fixtures before increasing throughput. Replay duplicate Stripe events, terminate a worker after upstream acceptance, delay a usage callback, exhaust a wallet during concurrent requests, and withdraw the cheapest permitted inference provider. Verify that funds are neither double-posted nor prematurely released, and that retry logic cannot cross tenant boundaries. For telecom, test a malformed prefix update, a destination-cost spike, a rejected campaign, and an abuse alert without sending unsolicited live traffic. Confirm that the system can stop new sessions while preserving evidence needed for customer support and applicable obligations. Zero-data-retention service requires an explicit data map spanning gateway logs, traces, crash reports, backups, and upstream providers; content-free operational metadata still needs defined access and retention rules. Publish an incident owner, escalation route, and recovery objective for each dependency. As an initial operating target, alert within five minutes of ledger mismatch and review unresolved balances within one business day, tightening these targets as service commitments require. Resume affected automation only after a reviewer checks reconciliation and the corrective change. Successful recovery means restored invariants, not merely a dashboard returning to green.

sections.heading: 1. Assign Fifteen Plays to Accountable Seats, Not Fifteen Specialists
paragraphs: Treat the 15 mapped plays as one controlled capacity book, not 15 businesses requiring separate teams. For seat allocation, use this chapter's operating decomposition: P01 H100 reservations, P02 H200 reservations, P03 B200 reservations, P04 supported GPU partition resale, and P05 GPU burst fulfillment form the compute lane. P06 multi-provider token routing, P07 batch inference, P08 dedicated endpoints, P09 inference failover, and P10 private zero-retention inference form the inference lane. P11 SIP origination, P12 SIP termination, P13 registered 10DLC messaging, P14 authorized IPv4 leasing, and P15 carrier overflow form the telecom lane. These identifiers organize the supplied opportunity scope; they are not additional scorecard revenue assumptions. Initially activate only plays whose support and accounting evidence the three-person pod can maintain. The founder, the single full-time seat, owns pricing, customer qualification, commitments, collections, and vendor negotiations. Contractor one owns compute reliability across P01 through P10; contractor two owns carrier operations across P11 through P15. The founder retains accountability for both lanes and the consolidated ledger. Give every play one accountable owner, a documented backup, an economic unit, and a suspension procedure before selling it. Capacity without a supportable operating owner stays outside the active catalog.

Buy contractor deliverables and bounded coverage rather than pretending two part-time specialists provide continuous human coverage. Illustrative procurement bands are $90-$140 per hour for GPU engineering and $70-$110 for carrier operations, with monthly hour ceilings and separately priced scheduled coverage. At the Conservative case, even two eight-hour monthly retainers at $100 and $85 consume $17,760 annually, leaving $52,740 of the $70,500 post-upstream expense envelope for every other modeled cost. That arithmetic rules out an unfunded round-the-clock promise. Use prepaid shutdown controls, upstream support, and explicit service windows instead. Contracts should identify deliverables, acceptance tests, response windows, invoicing evidence, security duties, and remediation of defective work. A priority-one incident receives acknowledgment within 15 minutes only during purchased coverage; outside coverage, automated containment runs and the published escalation schedule applies. Pay the fixed accepted-work fee first; any bonus should depend on collected contribution and measured quality, never merely GPU occupancy or terminated minutes. Require reproducible tests for routing changes, tenant isolation, wallet exhaustion, and carrier rollback. Worker status follows the actual relationship, including control and independence, rather than the contract heading. Review applicable classification requirements before imposing employee-like schedules on contractors.

Expand to two full-time seats and three contractors only when measured workload and contribution support the replacement capacity. The second full-time seat becomes service delivery and revenue operations lead, taking daily exceptions, customer onboarding, invoice reconciliation, and incident coordination away from the founder. The third contractor provides independent metering, security, and ledger QA; this person must not approve their own production changes. Existing compute and telecom contractors retain specialist execution. Track founder hours by sales, operations, and engineering for eight weeks before authorizing the hire, then verify those hours actually move. A useful internal hiring test is collected incremental contribution covering 1.5 times the added fully loaded monthly cost for three consecutive months, with six months of that cost reserved in unrestricted cash. These are management thresholds, not changes to the canonical Scaled case. That case allows $324,000 of annual post-upstream expenses before $456,000 owner profit. Fit the proposed staffing, software, insurance, support, and service-credit budget inside that envelope or publish a separate downside forecast. Maintain organization-owned repositories, vendor accounts, and recovery methods so the new lead can operate without borrowing the founder's personal identity or receiving shared administrator credentials.

callout.title: Make Specialist Knowledge Portable Before It Becomes Leverage
callout.body: The strongest small pod stores operational judgment in tested artifacts, not private contractor conversations.
items: Require the GPU contractor to attach DCGM samples, scheduler allocation IDs, and tenant-isolation results to each partitioning change; verify the exact GPU and software combination supports the promised configuration.
Keep LiteLLM routing policies and vLLM deployment manifests in organization-owned version control, with provider credentials injected from a secret store rather than copied into support tickets.
Pay telecom quality bonuses only after accepted SIP calls, customer disputes, and carrier invoices reconcile; raw minutes reward expensive low-quality routes and abuse.
Record a quarterly replacement drill in which the backup suspends a tenant, rotates scoped credentials, restores routing, and explains the resulting ledger entries without founder intervention.

sections.heading: 2. Run a Weekly Scorecard That Rewards Collected Quality
paragraphs: Publish one weekly scorecard by Monday noon using the preceding Sunday cutoff, with immutable source extracts and named exception owners. The founder reviews economic exposure; contractors explain controllable operating causes. For compute, separate reserved GPU-hours, allocatable hours, sold hours, delivered hours, and credited hours. Utilization means sold billable hours divided by committed allocatable hours, with maintenance treatment stated explicitly; it is not average GPU activity reported by DCGM. For inference, report contribution per million delivered tokens by model and provider, separately tracking input, output, cache, retry, and batch billing rules. Use LiteLLM request identifiers and provider usage records to reconcile customer charges, while vLLM throughput and latency metrics explain delivery quality. For telecom, measure contribution per accepted minute or message, answer-seizure ratio, average call duration, post-dial delay, and disputed usage by destination. Do not reward answer-seizure ratio improvements created by rejecting difficult legitimate destinations. Compare each metric with its contracted service target and a four-week baseline. A red metric requires an owner, quantified exposure, next action, and due date, rather than a narrative about traffic growth. Preserve definitions across weeks so a denominator change cannot masquerade as an operational improvement.

Set internal escalation thresholds before contractor bonuses are calculated. Investigate a meter-to-invoice difference above 0.5% of sampled billings, any confirmed cross-tenant exposure, or any spend exceeding an approved prepaid limit. Treat these as management controls; contractual remedies still follow the signed service terms. Wallet enforcement must reserve estimated cost before dispatch and settle actual usage afterward, because Stripe payment status alone cannot stop concurrent requests from overspending a balance. Bound in-flight GPU jobs, token requests, and SIP sessions; account for delayed carrier records, settlement reversals, and chargebacks. Suspend new dispatch when available credit cannot cover the maximum permitted exposure. For QA, sample at least five transactions per active play weekly and all manual adjustments, then increase sampling when errors cluster. Score contractor work using accepted changes, repeat incident frequency, evidence completeness, and response performance within purchased coverage. A proposed bonus pool of 5% of accepted monthly fees is an explicit expense, not an invisible deduction from customer credits. Do not withhold ordinary accepted fees because upstream pricing moved. The founder owns procurement risk; specialists own the measurable deliverables and operating controls they agreed to perform.

Enforce a 25% cap separately on customer concentration and upstream counterparty concentration, aggregating entities under common control. Measure customer concentration using both trailing-quarter gross billings and retained contribution; use the higher percentage for decisions. Measure supplier concentration using both trailing-quarter upstream spend and next-quarter noncancelable commitments. A routing dashboard showing four brands is insufficient when all four depend on one bare-metal owner or carrier group. Record underlying dependencies where contracts and supplier disclosures allow them to be established. A small launch book may breach the cap immediately because its first customer represents all sales. Label that condition a launch exception, limit irreversible commitments, diversify, and do not represent the book as meeting the mature operating standard. Once diversified, block incremental concentrated commitments until exposure falls within limits. Maintain at least four independent material counterparties where feasible, but do not force technically unsuitable traffic onto a provider just to improve a percentage. Test substitution with representative workloads and calls. A portable customer contract still has little value when its model behavior, number inventory, or latency requirement depends on one nontransferable upstream arrangement. Report the tested substitution cost beside each concentration measure.

sections.heading: 3. Close Accrual Books That Survive a Change of Owner
paragraphs: Reconcile the scorecard through three distinct layers: customer gross billings, retained contribution after upstream charges, and owner net profit after the remaining modeled expenses. Conservative produces $150,000 gross billings, $52,500 upstream cost, $97,500 retained contribution, $70,500 remaining expenses, and $27,000 owner profit. Base produces $675,000 gross billings, $236,250 upstream cost, $438,750 retained contribution, $249,750 remaining expenses, and $189,000 owner profit. Scaled produces $1,200,000 gross billings, $420,000 upstream cost, $780,000 retained contribution, $324,000 remaining expenses, and $456,000 owner profit. Owner profit divided by gross billings yields 18%, 28.0%, and 38%; divided by retained contribution it yields 27.69%, 43.08%, and 58.46%. The 65% retained-share convention is a scenario bridge, not proof that every contract receives identical ASC 606 presentation. Document principal-versus-agent conclusions by performance obligation, including control before transfer, fulfillment responsibility, inventory risk, and pricing discretion. An agent generally recognizes its fee rather than underlying pass-through billings; a principal may recognize gross revenue with corresponding cost of service. Never substitute customer model spending, carrier traffic value, or prepaid wallet deposits for earned operator revenue. Preserve both the management bridge and the reporting-policy reconciliation so buyers can compare contracts consistently.

Close by service month, not by the date Stripe transfers cash. Record unearned prepaid customer balances as contract liabilities until the corresponding service is delivered, subject to the applicable contract and accounting policy. Accrue upstream GPU reservations and carrier usage in the same period as delivery, including estimates for late carrier records with subsequent true-ups. Track committed but unused capacity separately so apparently healthy customer cohorts cannot conceal idle reservations. Cohorts should retain acquisition month, customer group, play identifier, provider, model or destination, contract term, and pricing version. Report gross billed usage, earned revenue under the documented presentation policy, retained contribution, service credits, refunds, chargebacks, and support burden without netting away operational failures. Reconcile opening wallet liability plus top-ups minus earned consumption, refunds, and other supported adjustments to the closing balance. Reconcile bank cash separately. A buyer inheriting prepaid balances inherits a delivery obligation, so sale proceeds cannot treat that cash as automatically surplus. Keep customer acquisition expense and recurring account service costs visible by cohort. The founder signs a monthly close checklist covering cutoff, accrual reversals, usage completeness, disputed invoices, deferred balances, and comparison with each canonical scenario's expense envelope.

Build transferability while contracts are still easy to negotiate. Obtain written copyright assignments signed by the rights owner for custom code and documentation under 17 U.S.C. section 204(a); do not assume contractor work automatically belongs to the company. Identify preexisting contractor tools, third-party licenses, model licenses, and open-source obligations separately because an assignment cannot transfer rights the contractor never owned. Customer and supplier agreements should specify assignment, change-of-control treatment, service credits, data handling, and responsibility for prepaid balances. Review actual transfer mechanics for numbers, messaging campaigns, address leases, and reserved hardware instead of assuming credentials are the asset. For voice operations, map the entity's actual role to 47 CFR sections 64.6301 and 64.6305, including applicable STIR/SHAKEN and Robocall Mitigation Database duties. Evaluate contribution and reporting obligations under 47 CFR sections 54.706 and 54.711 and current FCC Form 499 instructions. TCR registration is an industry messaging requirement, not a replacement for statutory calling or texting rules. Enforce authorization, AUP screening, tenant isolation, and promised zero retention. Provide buyers aggregated usage and redacted contracts first; move restricted customer records only through documented, authorized diligence procedures.

sections.heading: 4. Value Transferable Earnings, Then Choose Exit or Distribution
paragraphs: Price the business on an explicit earnings definition before discussing a multiple. Owner net profit in the scorecard is not automatically seller's discretionary earnings or adjusted EBITDA. Build a bridge from reported results to normalized earnings, identifying owner compensation already expensed, genuine nonrecurring costs, recurring contractor work, and the cost of replacing founder labor. Do not add back an essential engineer merely because they invoice as a contractor. For an illustrative Base acquisition, assume the $189,000 owner profit requires an additional $90,000 annual replacement manager cost that is not already included in modeled expenses. Transferable earnings then equal $99,000. Applying an underwriting range of 2.5 to 4.0 times those earnings implies $247,500 to $396,000 of enterprise value. This is a negotiating model, not an observed comparable-sales claim. If management cost already sits in the expense ledger, deduct only the incremental replacement requirement. A small owner-operated buyer might instead analyze SDE and personally perform the founder role, but their multiple and debt capacity must match that labor assumption. Present both labor bridges clearly rather than selecting whichever produces the largest headline price. Substantiate every add-back with invoices, payroll records, or contracts.

For the Scaled case, assume the $456,000 owner profit still requires $120,000 of incremental founder replacement cost beyond expenses already modeled. That leaves $336,000 of illustrative transferable earnings. A 3.0 to 4.5 times underwriting range produces $1,008,000 to $1,512,000 of enterprise value. The higher range requires evidence of renewal behavior, durable contribution after hardware repricing, low concentration, transferable commitments, clean ownership, and operation without founder escalation. It does not follow simply from using H200 or B200 hardware. Stress the book by reducing gross billings 10% while holding upstream commitments and other modeled expenses fixed: Base owner profit falls from $189,000 to $121,500, and Scaled falls from $456,000 to $336,000 before additional replacement costs. These are downside sensitivities, not revised canonical cases. At Conservative scale, $27,000 owner profit supports little independent management capacity; a buyer may prefer a customer-book or asset purchase. Translate enterprise value into expected proceeds by addressing debt, cash treatment, working capital, prepaid obligations, transaction costs, escrow, and contingent consideration. Avoid counting wallet obligations twice if they are already included in the agreed working-capital mechanism. Value an earnout by its measurable collection conditions, not its advertised maximum.

Run an exit rehearsal before hiring a broker. For 30 days, have the service lead or designated backup conduct daily operations while the founder performs only documented commercial exceptions. Log every intervention and repair the underlying dependency. Assemble a controlled diligence room containing monthly accrual statements, cohort contribution, concentration schedules, signed contracts, IP assignments, incident summaries, supplier commitments, regulatory responsibility records, and tested recovery procedures. Use redacted configuration inventories rather than live secrets, customer prompts, call content, or unrestricted traffic records. Ask prospective buyers to specify earnings treatment, replacement staffing, working capital, transfer conditions, and payment certainty in their proposals. Compare expected net proceeds with retaining the business, reserving capital for renewals and disputes, and distributing only genuinely surplus cash. A durable cash cow still needs refreshed GPU pricing, carrier quality reviews, customer diversification, and contractor backup; harvesting is not abandonment. Keep the same weekly scorecard whether selling or holding. When the pod can produce accurate books, enforce prepaid exposure, and recover service without the founder, the owner gains two credible options: accept a well-supported transfer price or retain a controlled stream of distributions. That operational choice is more valuable than a multiple attached to unverifiable gross traffic.

chapters.executive_summary: Candidate #36, GPU Compute & Telecom Capacity Arbitrage, ranks #03 of 36 with a 94/100 Money-to-Manpower Score. This sprint turns 15 mapped plays into a sequenced backlog, not fifteen simultaneous businesses. One full-time operator and two contractors validate one GPU offer, one inference route, and a separately qualified telecom lane. Days 1–30 establish prepaid demand, supplier economics, isolation, metering, and reversible capacity commitments. The canonical annual owner profits are $27,000 Conservative, $189,000 Base, and $456,000 Scaled; gross billings are $150,000, $675,000, and $1,200,000. A 65% retained share separates supplier pass-through from operator economics. Day-30, Day-60, and Day-90 decisions combine collected revenue, utilization, service evidence, and cash runway. Unproven demand earns a bounded repair cycle, never an automatic hardware commitment.

sections.heading: 1. Days 1–7: Price the Fifteen-Play Backlog Before Renting Capacity
paragraphs: Begin with a working execution map for Candidate #36's fifteen plays, rather than treating every available capacity spread as a launch product. P01 is reserved H100 resale; P02, H200 memory premium resale; P03, B200 performance premium resale; P04, supported NVIDIA MIG slice packaging; P05, scheduled batch GPU windows; and P06, interruptible GPU capacity. P07 is multi-provider inference routing; P08, asynchronous inference batches; P09, dedicated private inference endpoints; and P10, inference overflow and failover. P11 is wholesale outbound SIP routing; P12, inbound DID and SIP capacity packaging; P13, registered 10DLC messaging capacity; P14, authorized IPv4 capacity leasing; and P15, secondary-carrier telecom failover. These labels are this chapter's operational decomposition of the supplied edge areas, not fifteen independently scored investments. Open P01 and P07 as the initial commercial experiments; substitute P02 only when a buyer's measured memory requirement justifies it. Keep P11–P15 in supplier and customer discovery until their separate operating requirements are satisfied. Every play receives a buyer, upstream resource, billing unit, minimum commitment, cancellation rule, and evidence link. An attractive catalog price without these fields cannot become a purchase order. This prevents a three-person pod from confusing a broad market map with executable weekly capacity.

Assign the full-time operator forty scheduled hours weekly across customer discovery, pricing, collections, supplier negotiation, and incident ownership. Budget contractor A twelve hours for infrastructure, LiteLLM, vLLM, DCGM, and tenant isolation; budget contractor B eight hours for carrier onboarding, telecom classification, abuse review, and reconciliation. These are sprint allocations, not assumptions that contractors provide continuous coverage. Require a named upstream escalation contact and sell only a support window the pod can actually cover. Use a shared issue board with a maximum of three active implementation tasks. During the first week, complete ten buyer interviews and request three written upstream offers, including a cancellable alternative. Record hardware generation, region, interconnect, available MIG profiles, driver constraints, permitted resale, and termination exposure. For telecom, record destinations, billing increments, number rental, failed-call charges, campaign charges, fraud limits, and supplier suspension rights. The operator owns pricing decisions; contractor A owns reproducible benchmarks; contractor B owns documented carrier requirements and ledger exceptions. A contractor's completed ticket is evidence of work, not permission to activate an untested customer route. Finish Day 7 with one signed pilot scope or a dated buyer objection that changes the next week's experiment.

Make the scorecard bridge explicit before discussing margins. Conservative gross billings of $150,000 less $52,500 upstream cost leave $97,500 retained revenue; $70,500 remaining costs leave $27,000 owner profit. Base gross billings of $675,000 less $236,250 upstream cost leave $438,750 retained revenue; $249,750 remaining costs leave $189,000 profit. Scaled gross billings of $1,200,000 less $420,000 upstream cost leave $780,000 retained revenue; $324,000 remaining costs leave $456,000 profit. Those profits equal 18%, 28.0%, and 38% of gross billings, or 27.69%, 43.08%, and 58.46% of retained revenue. The supplied monthly opex range of $2,000–$14,000 cannot represent every residual cost in every case: Base remaining costs average $20,812.50 monthly. Maintain separate fixed, variable, labor, and other cost lines rather than silently forcing the totals together. Use the supplied 65% retained share for comparison, while documenting actual ASC 606 principal-versus-agent treatment by contract. Prepaid wallet balances are liabilities until service is earned, not immediate revenue. Set a $6,000 first-month launch exposure ceiling, including noncancelable obligations, excluding refundable customer funds. With only $10,000 available capital, reduce that ceiling further whenever the remaining cash fails the runway test.

callout.title: Buy the Customer's Bottleneck, Not the Newest Accelerator
callout.body: Preserve the option to change suppliers until the customer's workload, payment behavior, and service requirements are measured.
items: Benchmark the buyer's actual context length and concurrency; a cheaper GPU-hour can produce a more expensive successful request.
Ask suppliers to align reservation start times with funded customer windows; unused setup days consume the same commitment as productive days.
Price telecom from completed destination-specific records, including rounding and surcharges; a headline domestic minute rate hides route-level losses.
Require written resale rights and supported isolation profiles before selling MIG capacity; hardware capability alone does not establish contractual permission.

sections.heading: 2. Days 8–14: Build Prepaid Metering and Prove the Service Boundary
paragraphs: Build the prepaid control loop before exposing an endpoint. Stripe collects payment, but an internal double-entry wallet ledger controls available service credit. Verify webhook signatures, deduplicate event identifiers, and reconcile payments, refunds, disputes, holds, and earned usage daily. A successful client redirect cannot fund a wallet; server confirmation must establish the payment state. Keep payment processing fees outside upstream capacity cost so the 65% retained-share bridge remains readable. Before each inference request, reserve credit against its bounded maximum output, then settle actual metered usage and release the difference. For GPU rentals, authorize a short rental window and stop renewal before credit exhaustion. For SIP, combine wallet checks with duration limits, destination restrictions, concurrency limits, and a supplier-side spend ceiling. Keep a separate allowance for delayed carrier records rather than pretending usage arrives instantly. Never finance launch payroll from refundable, unearned customer balances. By Day 10, replay duplicate webhooks, delayed records, payment reversals, and exhausted balances in a test tenant. The completion criterion is zero duplicate credit and zero unbounded exposure, not merely a successful payment screen. The operator signs the reconciliation while contractor A retains reproducible test evidence for every failure case.

Instrument each service with the correct denominator. DCGM reports GPU health and utilization; it does not independently prove customer billable time or model token counts. Join scheduler leases, tenant identifiers, wall-clock allocation, and provider invoices for GPU billing. For inference, record model version, input tokens, output tokens, retries, cache treatment, and upstream charges under a stable request identifier. Configure LiteLLM routes and vLLM limits so a fallback cannot silently change the promised region, model quality, or data handling. Restrict private-endpoint P09 and failover P10 until those constraints survive fault tests. Test tenant isolation with separate credentials, network policies, storage permissions, and supported GPU partitioning; MIG is not a replacement for the surrounding isolation design. Disable prompt and response logging wherever a zero-data-retention contract requires it, and verify the upstream provider's retention terms independently. Preserve content-free usage metadata only within the agreed scope. Benchmark P05 and P08 with restartable batch jobs before offering interruption-sensitive P06 capacity. A single cross-tenant read, exposed credential, or unauthorized content log stops the affected service immediately. Performance tuning resumes only after containment, credential rotation where needed, and a repeatable passing isolation test.

Treat telecom readiness as a separate workstream rather than copying GPU onboarding. Contractor B documents whether the operator is acting as a voice service provider, intermediate provider, reseller, messaging participant, or capacity lessor for each offer. Apply the relevant STIR/SHAKEN and Robocall Mitigation Database requirements under 47 CFR 64.6301 and 64.6305 to that role; buying authenticated wholesale termination does not erase the operator's own obligations. Determine FCC Form 499-A registration, reporting, contribution, and exemption treatment from the actual services and current official instructions. Do not equate an exemption from one contribution obligation with exemption from every filing. For P13, complete the applicable carrier and Campaign Registry brand and campaign process, then separately implement the calling and texting requirements relevant under 47 U.S.C. 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200. Registration does not authorize unwanted messages. Restrict trial traffic to documented customer-controlled destinations, with suppression handling and abuse escalation tested. For P14, verify address-holder authority, leasing rights, routing authorization, and reputation history before listing inventory. Day 14 may legitimately conclude with compute ready and telecom still in qualification. The pod should report that difference plainly instead of manufacturing a unified launch status.

callout.title: Four Verifications Before Any Paid Production Traffic
callout.body: A failed check blocks the affected service, not unrelated discovery work. Retest the exact failure before restoring traffic.
items: Payment verification: duplicate and reordered payment events produce no duplicate credit; all usage paths stop within the documented prepaid exposure allowance.
Service verification: cross-tenant access tests pass, credentials are scoped, and promised retention and regional restrictions survive provider failover.
Economic verification: quoted upstream expense includes idle commitments and remains at or below 35% of eligible gross billings under the tested workload.
Telecom verification: applicable provider filings, campaign onboarding, lawful traffic requirements, destination limits, and supplier escalation responsibilities are documented before activation.

sections.heading: 3. Days 15–21: Sell Bounded Pilots and Measure Earned Contribution
paragraphs: Sell a prepaid pilot with a measurable workload and an explicit end date, not an unlimited discounted account. For P01, specify GPU generation, allocated hours, storage, egress, interruption treatment, and benchmark acceptance. For P07, specify model set, context limits, output caps, latency measurement, eligible regions, and whether retries are billable. Let P02–P06 and P08–P10 enter the active backlog only when a pilot reveals a priced requirement. A request for larger memory can support P02; a vague interest in newer hardware cannot support P03. For telecom, activate P11 or P13 only after the preceding checks pass, and keep P12, P14, and P15 tied to specific buyer requirements. Require verifiable customer identity, intended use, and an enforceable acceptable-use schedule. Review suspicious destination patterns, abrupt GPU saturation changes, and resale behavior against that schedule; crypto-mining is a stop condition when the contract prohibits it, not merely because utilization is high. The operator owns two pilot relationships at most during this week. Contractor A handles one reproducible technical issue queue, while contractor B reviews identity, traffic purpose, and supplier exceptions. This keeps customer learning inside the pod's actual support capacity.

Translate the 65% retained-share target into a reservation test. Let C be the committed supplier cost for a period, H the available sellable hours, p the realized customer price per hour, and v the variable upstream cost per sold hour. At utilization u, upstream expense is C plus H times u times v, while gross billings are H times u times p. To keep upstream expense within 35% of billings, utilization must reach C divided by H times the quantity 0.35p minus v. Use parentheses in the spreadsheet so the entire product is the denominator. A nonpositive denominator or a required utilization above 100% rejects the offer at that price. Illustratively, a $700 weekly reservation, 168 sellable hours, $20 realized hourly price, and $0.50 variable upstream hourly expense require 64.1% utilization. These inputs are a worked pricing example, not a market quote or a replacement scorecard. At 70% utilization, billings are $2,352, upstream cost is $758.80, and retained contribution is $1,593.20, or 67.74%, before payment fees, labor, support, and other expenses. Recalculate whenever discounts, credits, hardware prices, or reservation lengths change.

Close the pilot ledger daily using earned service rather than wallet deposits. Record gross usage charges, service credits, upstream consumption, allocated idle commitments, processor fees, refunds, support time, and attributable contractor expense. Present owner-profit estimates only after remaining operating costs are included using a consistent scorecard policy. Track replacement labor separately as a sensitivity rather than silently changing the canonical owner-profit definition. For SIP, reconcile call detail records by destination and billing increment; for messaging, include carrier and campaign charges; for IPv4, include rights, provisioning, and reputation-related support costs. Calculate service success on eligible attempts, count retries explicitly, and distinguish an upstream failure from a client-invalid request. Adopt a 99.5% technical success objective for the pilot and test latency against the customer's written p95 budget. Neither metric should be marketed as a contractual service level without matching remedies and supplier support. By Day 21, complete at least two funded pilot evaluations, even if only one becomes recurring demand. If no buyer funds a pilot, document offer, price, decision-maker, objection, and next decision date. The expected one-to-four-month first-deal window makes weak early conversion a bounded sales repair problem, not evidence that idle reservations should be enlarged.

sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30 and Reviews at 60/90: Kill Exposure, Fix Evidence, Scale Demand
paragraphs: Close the month against a cash plan, not a dashboard of deposits. Allocate the illustrative $6,000 launch ceiling across $1,800 cancellable capacity and benchmarks, $2,000 contractor work, $600 telemetry and payment tooling, $600 service-specific onboarding, and $1,000 contingency. These are spending limits, not supplier quotations. Count a noncancelable future payment against exposure when signed; avoid counting it twice when paid. Calculate runway as unrestricted cash after refundable balances, taxes payable, and termination obligations, divided by the greater of current weekly cash burn or unavoidable weekly operating payments. Require eight weeks after any proposed commitment. A $10,000 capitalization does not automatically permit spending $6,000: if the remainder cannot cover that runway, reduce experiments and commitments first. Keep an additional refundable-customer-balance register rather than assuming all Stripe cash is deployable. Days 22–29 reconcile every supplier minimum, contact each pilot buyer, complete at least twenty cumulative qualified discovery conversations, and issue at least five priced proposals. Measure operator support load against a ten-hour weekly ceiling and contractor work against the twelve-hour and eight-hour allocations. Persistent overtime means the offer needs simplification before the next customer is accepted.

Apply Kill before Fix before Scale at every review. Kill means suspend the affected service or stop new commitments while completing orderly customer obligations; it does not mean abandon existing contracts. Immediately stop affected traffic for cross-tenant exposure, prohibited use, missing required service authority, or unbounded prepaid leakage. Stop new reservations when projected runway falls below eight weeks or when achievable pricing cannot produce positive contribution after upstream and direct variable delivery costs. Day-30 Scale requires two paying organizations, at least $3,000 collected and earned billings over the preceding fourteen days, 65% retained contribution, and a costed owner-profit model of at least 18% of gross billings. Require 99.5% technical success, meter variance no greater than 1%, and two successful wallet-exhaustion tests. Committed GPU utilization must exceed both 55% and the calculated 65%-retention utilization floor; other lanes use their own contribution and prepaid-exposure tests. Passing permits only one additional paid pilot and at most a 25% increase in cancellable capacity. Missing a commercial threshold without a hard failure triggers Fix: assign one owner, one hypothesis, a fourteen-day deadline, and at most $1,000 additional exposure within the continuing runway limit.

At Day 60, require four paying organizations, $22,500 collected and earned trailing-thirty-day gross billings, 65% retained contribution, and at least 18% actual owner-profit margin after the full period's operating costs. Require repeat purchase from at least half of customers eligible to renew and cap the largest customer at 50% of billings. GPU commitments must exceed both 65% utilization and their retention floor. Day-90 Scale requires six paying organizations, $56,250 trailing-thirty-day gross billings, 65% retained contribution, and 28% owner-profit margin: $36,562.50 retained revenue and $15,750 profit, matching Base monthly arithmetic without claiming a completed year. Require 70% eligible-customer repeat purchase, no customer above 35% of billings, and GPU utilization above both 70% and its retention floor. Carry forward the service, meter, support, wallet, and runway tests. A second consecutive missed repair deadline stops the affected offer's new spending. Zero funded pilots by Day 90 after fifty qualified conversations and ten priced proposals also stops that offer; a documented procurement milestone may justify a cash-capped wait without capacity purchases. Expand toward the Scaled case only with the separate 2 FT + 3 C staffing plan and contracted demand. The fifteen-play backlog remains sequenced by evidence, not by catalog completeness.
